options: A screening tool for peripheral artery disease (PAD). Measure systolic blood pressure in both arms and both ankles. Use the highest arm systolic pressure as the denominator. Example: Right arm = 160/80 mmHg, left arm = 120/60 mmHg; right ankle = 120/60 mmHg, left ankle = 80/40 mmHg. Right ABI = 120 ÷ 160 = 0.75. Left ABI = 80 ÷ 160 = 0.50. The lower ABI is the left leg (0.50), indicating the left leg has a higher risk/severity of PAD.
questions.correctAnswer: A screening tool for peripheral artery disease (PAD). Measure systolic blood pressure in both arms and both ankles. Use the highest arm systolic pressure as the denominator. Example: Right arm = 160/80 mmHg, left arm = 120/60 mmHg; right ankle = 120/60 mmHg, left ankle = 80/40 mmHg. Right ABI = 120 ÷ 160 = 0.75. Left ABI = 80 ÷ 160 = 0.50. The lower ABI is the left leg (0.50), indicating the left leg has a higher risk/severity of PAD.
questions.explanationText: ABI is calculated by dividing the ankle systolic pressure by the highest brachial (arm) systolic pressure. An ABI of 1.00–1.40 is generally normal, 0.91–0.99 is borderline, 0.41–0.90 suggests PAD, and ≤0.40 indicates severe PAD. In this example, the left ABI is 0.50 and the right ABI is 0.75, so both legs are abnormal, with the left leg showing more significant arterial disease.  If below 0.4 it is concerning!!!!
